To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the contraction of isolated esophageal muscle in response to ACH is mediated by a protein kinase C dependent pathway, that the pathway is dependent upon extracellular calcium, and that calcium is required primarily to activate phospholipase C.
ACh-induced Ca2+ influx and PKC activation are required for acetylcholinesterase contraction of cat esophagus circular smooth muscle cells.
ACh-induced contractions of isolated cat esophageal muscle depend upon Ca2+ entry through voltage-gated Ca2+ channels and activation of PKC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Ca2+ in the contractile response of isolated cat esophageal muscle.
elucidating the mechanisms involved in the regulation of the contractile activity of smooth muscle.
the mechanisms by which the esophageal muscle contracts and relaxes, and with how the muscle contracts and relax in response to food in the esophagus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the contraction of the esophageal circular muscles cells is dependent on the extracellular calcium and PKC.

Ca2+ is required for ACh-induced contraction, that Ca2+ may not be required for contraction in response to ionic Ca2+, and that Ca2+ influx may be required to activate the phosphatidylcholine phospholipase C, which is the source of the diacylglycerols that are the activators of PKC.
Ca2+ is not a necessary cofactor for contraction induced by 1,2 DAG in esophageal circular smooth muscle cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Ca(2+), which is required for the ACh-induced contraction, may be needed to activate the phosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase C, but not the diacylglyceride lipase, and to activate PKC, which is the effector for contraction.
calcium is required for acetylcholin-induced contraction of esophagea circular muscle cells.
Ca2+ is required for contraction induced by ACh but not for contraction induced by DAG.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calcium is necessary for contraction in response to acetycholine.
Ca2+ is required for the contraction of the circular muscle cells in the esophagus.
calcium is necessary for the contraction of smooth muscle cells in the esophagus.
